title: Cerebra Analytics POC Scoping - Open Models
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on model shortlist (open models), success criteria (latency, accuracy on domain docs), workload sizing and benchmarking plan. Customer needs bilingual support (English + Spanish) and some Mandarin coverage; data privacy / PHI concerns push toward VPC or isolated Dedicated. Agreed 2-week POC timeline with Redwood to run benchmarks on 3 candidate open models and provide performance/quality matrix.
next_steps: Redwood: send POC proposal + pricing + security one-pager (Maya) - due 2026-04-02
SE: share benchmark template and sample prompts (Julian) - due 2026-04-01
Customer: provide representative prompt set and 2 weeks of anonymized sample docs (Dr. Lina) - due 2026-04-03
Schedule follow-up technical check-in after baseline benchmarks (week of 2026-04-06)
action_items: Maya Patel: send proposal + security docs; due 2026-04-02
Julian Rivera: prepare benchmark harness and baseline scripts; due 2026-04-01
Dr. Lina Chen: upload de-identified sample dataset + evaluation criteria; due 2026-04-03
Arjun Mehta: confirm VPC/network constraints and auth method (SAML) with infra team; due 2026-04-05
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-31 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 55 mins
Attendees: Maya P (Redwood AE), Julian R (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Chen (Cerebra Head of ML), Arjun M (Platform), Sophie P (Product)

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, we pulled together julian our se; quick check, is this still a good time?
00:06 - Dr. Lina: yes, thanks. we've been looking at open models for annotation and document QA, want to scope a short poc to see perf/cost and accuracy on our medical shipping notes, and a multilingual subset (spanish).
00:15 - Maya: great, that's helpful. julian and i will run through how we typically run a 2-week poc, the model shortlist we suggest for open models, and then dig into success criteria and workload sizing.
00:26 - Julian: hi team. quick note — from what you described, key variables for perf are sequence length, qps spikes, and whether you need streaming. also domain quality for medical terminology will drive which model we pick.
00:39 - Sophie: correct; product wants sub-300ms token latency when possible, and at least 95% recall on our named-entity extraction for key fields. if latency is much higher, customer UX suffers.
00:50 - Arjun: to add, our infra team prefers VPC or dedicated capacity for PHI. we have SAML SSO and KMS (aws-kms) already in place. question — can redwood run in our VPC or do we need to ship data to hosted?
01:03 - Maya: yes, we support both hosted and private deployment. for a POC we can run benchmarks on our hosted infra with isolated datasets, or spin up a private evaluation environment (Redwood Dedicated or Private) — both are options. we'll include that in the proposal.
01:16 - Dr. Lina: ok. on models: we want to emphasize open models. what would you recommend? we've seen llama2, mistral, falcon mentioned.
01:25 - Julian: typical shortlist for this use case: Llama-2-13B-chat (good baseline for chat style QA), Mistral-Instruct-7B (better instruction tuning, smaller footprint), and Falcon-40B-Instruct for stronger few-shot quality — though 40B increases infra cost. another candidate is MPT-30B if you want long-context. note: license checks matter for production.
01:44 - Sophie: are there quant/quantization options? cost is a big concern.
01:48 - Julian: yes, quantization profiles — 8-bit or mixed int8 / int4 depending on fidelity — can reduce cost significantly. Redwood Optimize will recommend safe quant profiles per model for your fidelity target. but for the baseline we'll run float32 or bfloat16 runs to measure accuracy, then quantized runs for cost numbers.
02:05 - Dr. Lina: multilingual — Spanish is primary second language, sometimes Mandarin — how do these models compare?
02:11 - Julian: Llama2 tends to be decent on Spanish, weaker on Mandarin depending on variant. Mistral's instruction models are comparatively strong on European languages; Falcon-40B tends to be good across multi-langs but the 40B footprint is heavy. If Mandarin is critical, we may consider specialist models or fine-tuning.
02:26 - Arjun: example workload: typical request is 1-2k tokens per doc, peak QPS ~6, baseline QPS 1. can you size the POC infra?
02:36 - Julian: for baseline bench, we suggest a 2-GPU setup per model variant for parallel runs — benchmarks will measure latency P50/P95 for your sequence lengths and batching behavior. for peak testing we'll emulate burst to 6 QPS and test batching policies. also we'll test KV cache reuse if you're doing conversational flows.
02:55 - Sophie: success criteria recap: latency <300ms token? or <300ms per request? we need clarity.
03:02 - Maya: yeah let's be precise in the doc. proposal will ask you to confirm: target p50 latency per token (or per 512-token generation) and an accuracy threshold on your NER/QA metrics. many customers set both a latency SLO and a quality pass rate.
03:15 - Dr. Lina: for us: p50 generation latency for a 512-token sequence under 2s, p95 under 5s, and entity extraction F1 > 0.92 on the holdout set. cost target is <$0.02 per 1k tokens if possible.
03:31 - Julian: noted. we'll run quality evals (exact-match / F1) vs your sample prompts. our baseline will include: 1) Llama-2-13B-chat float run; 2) Mistral-Instruct-7B float run; 3) Falcon-40B-Instruct float run (or Falcon-40B-int8 if memory constrained) — compare quality + latency + cost.
03:52 - Arjun: network/security — we need SAML SSO for console access, audit logs, and KMS support for key management. we also need to know data retention and model telemetry.
04:03 - Maya: we will attach SOC2 one-pager and our security deck. Redwood supports SAML/SSO and customer-managed KMS in Private. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available in Redwood Console. retention policies can be configured for the POC.
04:15 - Sophie: timeline?
04:17 - Maya: we typically do: week 1 baseline benchmarks + quality evals, week 2 integration + a performance run in your preferred network mode (hosted isolated vs dedicated). so a 2-week POC is feasible if we get data and access quickly.
04:29 - Dr. Lina: sounds good. what about benchmarks artifacts? we want the raw numbers and the scripts so we can reproduce locally.
04:36 - Julian: we'll share the benchmark harness on github (link) and a spreadsheet with p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics per model. we will also provide run commands so your infra team can replicate.
04:48 - Arjun: any gotchas on tokenization or prompt engineering for medical text?
04:52 - Julian: yes — medical shorthand and OCR artifacts can confuse tokenizers. we'll include normalization steps and provide a small prompt set that helps steer models. also consider a small domain fine-tune or instruction-tuning pass if baseline quality is low; that's typically a follow-up.
05:08 - Maya: ok to recap next steps — we'll send proposal + security docs (maya), se will share benchmark harness and sample prompt template (julian), and you will share de-identified samples and evaluation goals (lina). we'll aim to kick off baseline bench the week of 2026-04-06.
05:23 - Dr. Lina: perfect, thanks everyone.
05:26 - Sophie: thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional transcript errors: "Falcon-40B" was sometimes transcribed as "Falcon forty be"; "KV cache" as "K V cash"; "SAML" occasionally appears as "samel". References shared: benchmark harness (github link), Redwood security deck (link), preliminary POC proposal (to be sent).
notes: Customer is PHI-sensitive - prefer VPC/Dedicated for production; POC can be either hosted isolated or dedicated evaluation environment
Customer target quality metric: NER F1 > 0.92; latency targets: p50 512-token <2s, p95 <5s
Shortlist models to benchmark: Llama-2-13B-chat, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-40B-Instruct (consider MPT-30B if long-context needed)
Plan: 2-week POC (week1 benchmarks + evals, week2 integration + perf runs)
Deliverables: benchmark harness, spreadsheet with p50/p95/cost/quality, security docs, proposal
